findings.issue: Legitimate `dispatch-claude.js <build-role> ... -w` dispatch is false-refused under default enforce. `-w` is documented as valid isolation, but `runCwd` remains `AGENT_ROOT` and the contract sees canonical cwd, so `validateDispatchForClass(build_chain_worker)` exits 1 before Claude can create its worktree. Reproduced with `builder - -w`: `dispatch_contract_violation` on canonical cwd.
findings.fix: Teach the contract request that `-w` means CLI-managed worktree isolation, or skip/alter the cwd_policy check when `passW` has already satisfied the wrapper isolation gate. Keep strict cwd validation for `--worktree <path>`.

findings.issue: Generic `fixer` is still treated as a build-chain sentinel by docs and `BUILD_CHAIN_ROLES`, but `GENERIC_BUILD_IDS` only contains `builder`. Under default enforce, `dispatch-claude.js fixer ... -w` is refused as unknown role instead of being class-validated as `build_chain_worker`.
findings.fix: Either add `fixer` to `GENERIC_BUILD_IDS` and revalidate it via `validateDispatchForClass`, or remove generic `fixer` from live docs and build-chain sentinel sets if it is no longer a supported dispatch input.

findings.issue: Compatibility risk: `dispatch-agent.js` normalizes legacy names for provider selection, but passes the raw role to `validateDispatch`. If legacy inputs like `redteam`, `qa`, or `compliance` are still considered live dispatch aliases, the new default blocks them as unknown before provider execution.
findings.fix: Decide canonical-only vs alias-compatible dispatch. If alias-compatible, normalize before the contract/shape consult while preserving original role only where needed for user-facing telemetry.

parsed.summary: Default enforcement is not safe as-is. Registered cross-provider roles validate correctly, review-fallback is sanctioned and reaches spawn under ENFORCE, fail-open is preserved on contract read failure, and the contract report/master escapes work for the contract gate. The blocking regression is the `-w` cwd mismatch; the generic `fixer` path is a second documented false-refusal.
